signature: reads $? immediately after a pipeline; that captures the exit status of the pipeline's last stage (e.g. tail/grep/wc), not the command whose result was actually wanted
phrasings: trusting the exit code after piping a command through tail/grep/head/wc without PIPESTATUS or pipefail
"RUFF_EXIT=0" that was actually tail's exit code, not the linter's
detector: procedural, not a single regex (see bin/recur-gate.sh:check_diff) — an added line in a *.sh diff hunk contains a bare $? (not PIPESTATUS) where the same line or the immediately preceding added line contains an unguarded command pipe, and no `pipefail` has appeared earlier in that file's diff
evidence: fleet-rs AGENTS.md hard rule #3 ("$? after a pipe reads the WRONG command... violated 6x in the predecessor, twice more in zsh"); Speed-of-Thought-L8-Deep-Dive/11-THREE-MEMORY-LAYERS.md §4.2/§6.2 names this the canonical case for "prose transfers at ≈0" — documented, then re-violated 6x including in the message naming it; this session independently re-derived the same failure ("my RUFF_EXIT=0 was tail's exit code")
exemptions: the $? line itself uses PIPESTATUS[0] or PIPESTATUS[-1]
a `set -o pipefail` (or `set -eo pipefail` / `set -euo pipefail`) appears earlier in the same file, before the flagged pipe
the preceding line's pipe is `||` (boolean or), not a command pipe
